newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Suspect in Sri Lankan MP killing surrenders. [CORRECTED 05:39 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Suspect in Sri Lankan MP killing surrenders. [CORRECTED 05:39 GMT]

text.p: One of two key suspects in the killing of a Sri Lankan legislator has turned himself in to a Colombo judge, a police source said on Monday.

Mahinda Ratnatilleke, the main opposition party's candidate for mayor of the southern city of Ratnapura (corrects from "the ruling coalition's candidate"), surrendered on Sunday night at the home of the magistrate for Fort, the central part of Colombo, the Colombo police source said.
Ratnatilleke was remanded until Thursday when he is to be presented before the Ratnapura magistrate, the source said.
Officials of the police Criminal Investigation Department, who are probing the case, declined to comment.

Last Tuesday's killing of ruling People's Alliance lawmaker Nalanda Ellawala during a roadside quarrel with supporters of the main opposition United National Party (UNP), harked back to an age of political violence in the late 1980's.

The slaying sparked two days of riots last week in the gem mining town of Ratnapura, 80 kms (50 miles) southeast of Colombo. Pro-People's Alliance mobs set fire to scores of buildings owned by UNP supporters, but no one was hurt.
The other named suspect in the case, UNP legislator Susantha Punchinilame, was still at large, police said.
Police have offered a one-million-rupee ($17,500) reward for information leading to the arrest of either Punchinilame or Ratnatilleke.
Ellawala, the youngest member of Sri Lanka's 225-seat parliament and the scion of an influential political family, was cremated last Saturday in a funeral attended by an estimated 100,000 mourners.

Soon after the funeral, about 20 gunmen attacked and robbed a Chinese restaurant owned by a well-known UNP lawmaker in downtown Colombo, but police said it was not clear if this was related to the continuing unrest. No one was hurt.

Ellawala was killed the day before the deadline for filing nominations in the March 21 local government polls, the first UNP-People's Alliance election contest since 1994 when the alliance ended UNP's 17 years in power.
